results: A nonnegative invertible Hermitian full-duality form on a complex Banach domain is coercive, with explicit coefficient 1/(norm(inverse)+1). Positivity is constant along a continuous connected family of invertible Hermitian full-duality operators.

For any nonnegative Hermitian full-duality operator P, norm(P v)^2 is bounded by the real quadratic energy at v times norm(P). Complex phases recover the entire dual norm, without assuming norm attainment.

For EVERY real original period-two H-minus-one potential q, EVERY lower bound a of its actual full original spectrum bounds the original quadratic form below by a times the original normalized L2 energy, on EVERY vector of the full original H1 domain.
The actual lowest original physical label supplies that quadratic-form lower bound and is nonpositive for mean-zero potentials.

For EVERY real mean-zero original H-minus-one potential whose spectrum is bounded below by a, its EXACT original norm is bounded by 4*(abs(a)+1)*C, where C is fixed independently of q and defined using original Laplacian, inclusion and singular multiplication operator norms.

The ENTIRE original isospectral set, with no endpoint membership premise, has the common original H-minus-one bound 4*(abs(lambda_0(q))+1)*C. This follows from equality of the actual original canonical labels.

A new reusable theorem selects one arbitrarily large positive shift and one L2 bound before EVERY real unit-period H-minus-one potential in a specified norm ball, and constructs real L2 Miura lifts at that same shift.

Combining the original isospectral H-minus-one bound with the exact period-one extraction norm bound gives one common arbitrarily large shifted real Miura representation and one common L2 bound for EVERY member of the entire original isospectral set.
quantifiers_and_normalization: The native Rayleigh theorem accepts all real period-two original H-minus-one potentials. Mean zero is needed only for the native potential norm bound. Physical period one is needed only in the article wrappers.

The domain is the entire original H1 space. The full-dual realization is exactly the verified isometric original H-minus-one/H1 duality. The normalized Fourier pairing and physical pi*k derivative are unchanged.

The original isospectral set is defined by equality of actual full physical algebraic multiplicities on the entire original real mean-zero physical period-one H-minus-one domain. No endpoint assumption or substituted isospectral set is used.
The fixed constant C is 1+norm(Laplacian)+norm(domain inclusion)+norm(singular multiplication family)+norm(domain inclusion(constant one))^2. It is strictly positive and independent of the potential.
The common shift c can exceed any specified real A. The positive translation c^2 and the common L2 bound are chosen before the isospectral member and its real lift.
essential_remaining: Lemma 2.21 requires a UNIFORM ENDPOINT Fourier-Lebesgue norm bound under the endpoint gap hypothesis. The new uniform H-minus-one bound is a necessary dependency and does not prove that endpoint bound.

Transfer all common-shift real diagonal Dirac lifts to one ACTUAL real source isospectral set. The existing nonzero-frequency multiplicity identity is available; exclude frequency zero with the exact trace identity and a shift below the common lowest Hill energy.

Derive the needed compact original finite-p realization or a direct uniform weighted inverse estimate from verified source results. Existing source Hilbert isospectral compactness and weighted membership alone do not yet establish higher weighted norm compactness.
Apply the already proved uniform endpoint bootstrap and Appendix B compactness only after their actual uniform and compact hypotheses have been established.
Main Theorems 1.1, 1.3, 1.4, 5.1 and 5.9 remain unproved; actual original KdV Birkhoff maps, actual H-minus-one KdV flow and remaining spectral comparisons are still required.
